title: Globular Cluster Omega Centauri
explanation:
# Omega Centauri: A Cosmic Mystery

Imagine 10 million stars—each older than our Sun—crammed into a sphere 150 light-years wide, creating the brightest and largest star cluster orbiting the Milky Way at a distance of 15,000 light-years. What makes Omega Centauri truly puzzling is that unlike typical star clusters, it contains stars of different ages and chemical compositions, suggesting it may be the surviving core of a small galaxy that collided with our own millions of years ago. Recent observations from the Hubble Space Telescope have even uncovered hints of a massive black hole lurking at its center—a discovery that deepens the mystery of this ancient cosmic jewel.
